resources.string: How to play
Rules
Strategy
Levels
The goal
Move all 52 cards onto the four foundations at the top. Each foundation takes one suit, starting with the Ace and building up: A, 2, 3, all the way to the King. Finish all four and you have won.
The board

The seven columns in the middle are the tableau - this is where you do your work. The face-down pile is the stock; tap it to turn cards over one at a time onto the waste beside it. When the stock runs out, tap it again to turn the waste back over and go round again, as often as you like.
Which moves are legal

In the tableau, a card goes on a card one rank higher of the opposite colour: a red 8 on a black 9. Any sequence already in that order moves as one. Only a King may go into an empty column. A card that is uncovered can always go to its foundation, and you may take the top foundation card back down if you need it.
What the app does for you

Tap a card and it goes to the best legal place, or drag it where you want. Aces and safe cards go to the foundations by themselves unless you turn that off in Settings. Undo is unlimited, and Hint will always show you a move that keeps a win possible.
These are the well-known principles of Klondike. None of them is a secret and none is a guarantee - they are simply what tends to work.
Turn cards over first

Every face-down card is information you do not have. A move that flips one is almost always better than a move that does not, and the column with the most face-down cards is usually the one worth digging into.
Do not rush the foundations
A card sent up early cannot come back down to hold anything. Keep low cards in the tableau while they might still catch a card you need, and send them up once nothing needs them.
Empty a column with a plan
An empty column is the most valuable thing on the board, because only a King can fill it. Empty one when you have a King ready, or a King you can reach, rather than for its own sake.
Watch the whole stock, not just the waste
Drawing is free and the stock never reshuffles, so cycling through it costs nothing but moves. Watch what goes past: knowing a card is coming round again changes which move you should make now.
When you are stuck, go back
Undo costs you nothing but a move in the counter. If a deal dries up, walking back a few moves and taking the other branch is usually faster than hoping the stock saves you.

Every deal here was put through a computer before it reached you, and the level says what it took to win - or, at the top of the ladder, that nothing managed it. It is a measure of the deal, not of you.
Trivial
Wins by obvious moves alone: turn cards over, take what is offered, play the waste. Good deals to learn on, and the level opens with the ones that forgive the most mistakes.
Easy
Needs you to choose between obvious moves: dig into the deepest column, and hold a card back when something still needs it. Obvious moves alone are not enough here.
Medium
Needs a move that gains nothing on the spot - shifting part of a sequence to uncover the card beneath it. Setting up before you profit is what this level is about.
Hard
Needs a card taken back down from a foundation. Counter-intuitive, and often the only way through, which is why it sits this high.
Expert
Beyond every rule of thumb: these deals were won by search, and only just - one of the two solvers found a line and the other could not. Expect to back up often.
Insane

Nothing solved these, so nobody knows a winning line, including us. Some of them cannot be won at all: among the comparable deals a solver did settle, about one in ten turned out to be impossible, and these are the harder ones it could not settle. So a loss here may not be your fault - the deal may simply have had no way through. Play them for the fight rather than the record.
